governance.note: The nyiso-41 keeper config PLUS the nyiso-42 reconciled Iroquois winter spread, promoted after fixing its two blocking root causes at source. (1) The reconciled reference gains a measured Algonquin-Citygate monthly CEILING (rule #14): the AGT-weighted re-allocation of the SOM annual Iroquois-Transco spread out-priced the NE complex Z2 physically delivers into (Feb-2023 $13.21 vs measured $8.13; Jan-2024 $8.60 vs $7.68; Jan-2025 $18.60 vs $16.92); each month caps at Henry Hub + the measured NEISO basis row (the series the NEISO keeper itself prices on), floored at the committed flat construction, and the shaved scarcity excess re-enters as a year-round base differential water-filled into months with ceiling headroom so the measured SOM ANNUAL spread is preserved exactly - a reconciliation of three measured series, no fitted constant, forward-regenerable from forward basis seasonality. (2) dual_fuel_oil_reattribution restored to its documented NEISO-only spec (a harness wiring bug had enabled the gas->oil scoring relabel for every ISO passing --gas-hub-basis-daily): the relabel exists to match ISNE's EIA-930 fuel attribution, and the NYIS feed demonstrably does not attribute that way (Jan-2025 parity switching would relabel 0.80 TWh vs 0.031 TWh measured NYIS NG:OIL; 2023 shows 2.17 TWh NYIS OIL vs a 0.42 TWh EIA-923 oil class - static plant-primary attribution parity hours cannot reproduce in either direction), so the relabel scored a basis mismatch against the HARD C2 gas family - it WAS the run-42 C2-2025 -2.5% FAIL (the winter gas never left the dispatch). Dual-fuel PRICING physics (min(gas, oil) cap) unchanged. EFFECT: C2-2025 gas -0.1% PASS (42: -2.5% FAIL); C5a CO2 -2.3/-5.3/-3.7% all years PASS (41: 2024 -7.1% breach - the switch-hours' CO2 stays in the model total); Jan-2024 winter overshoot +6 -> +1.6; Feb-2023 and Jan-2025 respect the measured ceiling. C3a widens to -16.2/-15.4/-13.5% (41: -13.3/-13.4/-9.5) because the flat construction's year-round eastern premium was propping shoulder LMPs (the run-42 E1 finding) - a removed compensation, not a regression to chase (rule #1); the residual is the ledgered frontier below. C1/C4/C6 PASS unchanged; outage overlay historic/exogenous.

_open_items: (1) DATA-BLOCKED eastern-NY winter hub level (carried from run-41, verified: zero free Iroquois Z2 prints anywhere; NGI/ICE paywalled) - Dec-2024 (-14.4 monthly residual) and Dec-2025 (+6.3) winter levels are funded only by the SOM-annual re-allocation, not a measured monthly print; the open ask is a licensed Iroquois Z2 daily/monthly series or NYISO SOM per-hub monthly data. (2) The ledgered reserve-scarcity / competitive-offer-markup frontier (nyiso-28/29/31): east zones clear ~$20 vs actual ~$26 in shoulder months (implied marginal HR ~11 vs ~15); the static published reserve requirements (NYCA 2620/1310/655, East 1200, SENY 1100, NYC 1000/500 MW) never bind against idle-capacity headroom credit, and data/raw/NYISO-AS carries measured AS PRICES, not a measured condition-varying requirement - still data-blocked. (3) NEW (run-43 E1 decomposition): Upstate_West collapses to the wind margin (~$1.4, ~75% of Apr-2023 hours) behind the measured 1,450 MW Central-East TTC while the EIA-930 monthly reconciliation band pushes ~830 MW of the measured net imports through the upstate link (NYC/LI node links 1,000+1,200 MW cannot carry the measured net alone); real upstate held ~$22-25 via gross two-way tie flows (IESO/PJM arbitrage) a single external node cannot represent - per-interface measured flows/ratings (NYISO ATC_TTC external-interface postings or EIA-930 per-DIBA NYIS interchange) are the documented data ask; zonal load split and in-state volumes verified against measured (UW April share model 0.365 vs measured 0.356).
